chapter.title: Atomic and Nuclear Phenomena
chapter.scopeNote: Original condensed MCAT Physics, Mathematics and Research Reasoning lessons. Models and calculations use stated assumptions. Independent scientific review is pending; this is not exhaustive textbook coverage.

steps.text: Photoelectric emission occurs when photon energy can overcome the material’s work function. The ideal maximum electron kinetic energy is Kmax = hf - φ for frequencies above threshold.
At fixed above-threshold frequency, increasing intensity mainly increases the number of emitted electrons per time rather than their maximum kinetic energy.
Below threshold, increasing ordinary single-photon light intensity does not produce emission in this elementary model. Multiphoton regimes require additional assumptions and are outside this model.
Stopping-potential magnitude satisfies eVs = Kmax. Distinguish energy in electronvolts from voltage in volts and photon arrival rate from energy per photon.

steps.text: An atom absorbs a photon when the photon energy matches an allowed energy gap. A transition to a higher state increases the atom’s internal energy.
Emission occurs when a system loses energy to a photon with E = ΔE = hf. Discrete energy levels produce characteristic spectral lines rather than every possible photon energy.
Not every pair of levels has an equally allowed transition. Selection rules and transition probabilities matter; a level diagram alone does not determine relative line intensities.
A larger positive energy gap corresponds to a higher-frequency, shorter-wavelength emitted photon. The energy zero for the level diagram does not alter a transition gap.

lessons.title: Nuclear Binding Energy and Mass Defect

steps.text: A bound nucleus has lower mass than its separated constituent protons and neutrons. The mass defect corresponds to binding energy through E = Δmc².
Binding energy is the energy required to separate the nucleus into free nucleons. Energy released during formation is the same magnitude for the reverse ideal comparison.
Compare nuclear masses with nuclear constituent masses, or atomic masses with a consistent electron accounting. Mixing conventions can produce a spurious mass defect.
Binding energy per nucleon helps compare nuclear stability trends but is not by itself a complete reaction-rate or decay-mode predictor.

steps.text: Nuclear equations conserve charge and nucleon number with emitted particles accounted for. Alpha decay lowers mass number by four and atomic number by two.
In beta-minus decay, a neutron converts to a proton while an electron and an antineutrino are emitted. Nuclear mass number stays fixed and atomic number increases by one.
For a single exponential decay population, N = N0(1/2)^(t/t½). A half-life concerns a population probability, not a scheduled lifetime for each nucleus.
Activity is λN and has units decays per second. Fusion and fission can release energy when products have a lower total mass; reaction feasibility and rate also require the stated conditions.
